treatment_suggestions.title: Administer morphine for pain management
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient presents with STEMI and severe chest pain (NRS 7/10). Morphine is indicated for pain relief and to reduce myocardial oxygen demand.

treatment_suggestions.title: Administer ondansetron for nausea
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient reported nausea, which is a common side effect of morphine and can exacerbate discomfort. Ondansetron is a 5-HT3 antagonist effective for acute nausea.

treatment_suggestions.title: Continuous EKG monitoring during transport
treatment_suggestions.rationale: STEMI requires continuous cardiac monitoring to detect arrhythmias or changes in ST segments during transport to the hospital.

treatment_suggestions.title: Ensure patient in left lateral decubitus position
treatment_suggestions.rationale: This position can improve coronary perfusion and reduce myocardial ischemia during transport.

treatment_suggestions.title: Administer oxygen if saturation <94%
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Although current saturation is 98%, oxygen should be administered if saturation drops below 94% to ensure adequate oxygenation in STEMI.

drafted_journal: Situation: Chest pain radiating to left arm. Debut at 15:45. Background: 62-year-old male with hypertension, hyperlipidemia. No known ischemic heart disease. No allergies. Currently at grandchildren's home. Sudden onset of chest pain at rest. Self-called ambulance. Current: Alert, ACVPU. Ongoing vegetative symptoms. a: Free. b: Saturation 98% without oxygen. AF 22. c: Cold, pale. BP 167/88. HR 86. EKG shows ST elevations V1-V6. Action: Administered nitroglycerin (no effect). EKG sent to HIA at Södersjukhus. HIA directs to angiography. d: Severe central chest pain for 45 minutes, radiating to left arm. Nausea. Pain NRS 7/10. Action: Administered ondansetron for nausea. Administered 2.5 mg morphine for pain. Nitroglycerin administered (no effect). e: PVK/infusion line placed. Prehospital assessment: STEMI. Recommendation: Transport to SÖS (St. Göran) for urgent angiography. Priority 1. During transport: Good effect from morphine and ondansetron. Transport in left lateral decubitus position. Continuous EKG monitoring. Deff-plates on. HIA personnel meet at ambulance bay.
